catalog_quote: Word stress in Yuanga falls on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word. Since its placement is predictable it does not have a distinctive or phonemic function, but it does have a demarcative function in that its presence marks off one phonological word from another. From a phonetic point of view word stress is characterised by extra expiratory force which results in a lengthening of the vocalic nucleus of the stressed syllable. ... new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word (Gomen dialect); predictable, non-contrastive, demarcative; realised as greater intensity and vowel lengthening. Independently confirmed by Bril & Galliot 2022 sec. 2.2 p.12 for Zuanga-Yuanga as a whole: accent démarcatif, non contrastif, on the avant-dernière syllabe du mot prosodique, trochaic foot built from the right word edge.
new_statements.secondary_stress: No secondary stress described as such; compounds formed from two former phonological words retain two word stresses (e.g. /'mwa'kabu/ 'church'). At phrase level a 'demarcative accent' (higher pitch) falls on one word per phrase, normally the verb, its peak coinciding with that word's stressed syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: (i) A class of interrogatives (/a'nira/ 'how many?', /e'nira/ 'when?' etc.) has antepenultimate stress. (ii) In V.V or CV.V sequences stress may fall only on the first vowel, so words like /'haipo/ 'much', /'aiyu/ 'to inhabit' surface with antepenultimate stress; but /a/ as second vowel can bear stress (/ju'anga/ 'Yuanga', /e'amwa/ 'where?'). (iii) An aspirated onset in an unstressed syllable lengthens its vowel and can phonetically mask the stress position (/pethumeno/). Bril & Galliot 2022 summarise the shift as 'l'accent peut se déplacer sur une syllabe antepenultième d'un mot prosodique pour des raisons de poids syllabique'.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word (stem plus affixes; 1-3 pretonic syllables + stressed nucleus + one post-tonic syllable); described from isolated words and phrases of the Gomen (GOs) dialect, fieldwork Paita 1982-83. Phrase-level pitch accent treated separately (sec. 5.3.1).
new_statements.identity_note: Schooling 1992 describes the Gomen dialect (GOs, village of Paita near Kaala-Gomen) of Yuanga; he notes two other mutually intelligible dialects (Bondé/St Paul and Paimboas). Bril & Galliot 2022 treat the language as 'zuanga-yuanga' covering GOs, PA (Paimboa) and BO (Bondé) variants and give the same penultimate rule for the language as a whole. All fall under Glottolog yuag1237 / ISO nua (Glottolog name 'Yuaga').

sources.note: Sec. 2.2 'Accent' (p.12): 'En zuanga-yuanga, l'accent est démarcatif, non contrastif; il est associé à une montée de l'intensité sur la syllabe accentuée. Il se place sur l'avant-dernière syllabe du mot prosodique. Le pied est trochéique ('σs σw), et le calcul se fait à partir de la frontière droite du mot. L'accent peut se déplacer sur une syllabe antepenultième d'un mot prosodique pour des raisons de poids syllabique.' Covers GOs (Gomen), PA (Paimboa), BO (Bondé) variants.
